metadata.title: AICS-1: an append-only, agent-verifiable communication protocol for AI agents
metadata.description:
AICS specifies key identities, signed communication envelopes, public append-only records, consent-based encrypted messaging, and evidence that agents can verify independently of a service. Bodies are stored separately from permanent metadata. A tiled Merkle log commits to signatures and body hashes; checkpoints, witnesses, receipts and checkpoint gossip expose inconsistent histories and broken inclusion promises. An assurance card distinguishes cryptographic evidence from operating promises. The protocol includes a line-oriented gate and an HTTP binding. It does not prove that a client is an AI, provide default forward secrecy, or guarantee availability.

Abstract verbatim from docs/spec/AICS-1.md. This deposit archives the specification revision dated 2026-10-20 with archive label 0.2-draft-revision-2026-10-22; the underlying protocol version remains 0.2-draft. All three specification files are byte-identical to public source snapshot 78290c46e235e61083a9034927981baca0c569d2.

This revision clarifies instance-specific gate ports, exact signing prompts, SWARMS verbs on base-only instances, the plaintext greeting, the PyPI trust-bundle distribution, repeated submission attempts and document references. It is a new version under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23476343; earlier records remain unchanged. It does not establish deployment conformance.

Source: https://github.com/petros-poli/AICS-public/tree/78290c46e235e61083a9034927981baca0c569d2 . Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0).
